title: Sausage Egg & Cheese Sandwiches
subtitle: Station sandwiches with real structure—no soggy bottoms.
description: Breakfast at the station has to survive interruptions. This recipe is written for real timing, clear heat cues, and a workflow that keeps food hot while the board gets loud.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Sausage Egg & Cheese Sandwiches in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.instruction: Butter split buns and toast on a griddle or sheet pan under the broiler until golden. Hold warm on a tray. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 6 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Cook sausage + eggs
steps.instruction: Cook sausage until browned and 165°F internal. Scramble or fry eggs in batches—keep finished eggs covered on a warm tray. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Assemble sandwiches
steps.instruction: Build sausage, egg, and cheese on toasted buns. Wrap in foil for the line if serving in waves. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Hold and serve
steps.instruction: Hold wrapped sandwiches in a 200°F oven up to 20 minutes. Serve with hot sauce on the side. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
